designs.title: Vineyard
designs.why: From 3 m it reads well: the arched window, spaced grotesk heading and keyline give a calm, quiet structure, and the terraced vineyard sitting inside it on a white tee looks clean. Up close the problems show. The 'engraving' is really a 1–2 px dither or stochastic halftone at 300 DPI, roughly 85–170 micron dots. On a single screen on cotton that will plug in the dark leaves and cypresses and drop out across the pale distant hills and walls, so the print will look muddy and patchy, not crisp. Some areas are already mushy: the house, the vine rows and the far hills read as grey noise, not cut lines. The scene is also generic Tuscan postcard art, with nothing that makes it ours, which is thin for a $50 tee.
designs.fix: Rebuild the art for the screen. Turn the fine dither into true engraved line work, or at least a coarse halftone (about 40–45 lpi) with a minimum dot that holds and the light tones knocked out cleanly. That keeps the grapes, house and terraces crisp on press, not muddy.
